messages:
Evan: heads up — since ~02:00 ap-southeast1 is seeing nvme IOPS saturation that’s blocking GPU provisioning. GPUs are scheduling but never reach RUNNING, attaching times >3m. janitor-scan pods are at 100% io_wait.
infra-bot: [ALERT] region=ap-southeast1 metric=nvme_iops util>85% for 12m — triggered 3267894321.
Sara: can you paste iostat or similar pls?
Evan: pasting quick iostat from one affected host:
```
Device            r/s     w/s   rMB/s   wMB/s  avgrq-sz  avgqu-sz  await  svctm  %util
nvme0n1        120.3  3921.7    0.02    6.78     3.6      9.1   12.4   0.24  92.7
```
Evan: it's dominated by small random writes, avg request size tiny but queue depth huge.
Kyle: that pattern usually means a scan/cleanup walking millions of tiny files and doing stat/unlink. any top-level dirs to blame?
Monica: we had a failed job yesterday that left a container overlay with a stale cache layer. the janitor worker scans mountpoints and tries to clean per-container caches; looks like one path ballooned.
Evan: ran `du -sh /var/tmp/gpu-cache/*` quickly — one entry is `18T /var/tmp/gpu-cache/old-run-xyz (18M files)` which explains it.
Sara: ouch. suggestion: throttle janitor concurrency and schedule a bounded deletion job rather than letting it blast IOPS. we should also prevent GPU attach from being blocked by janitor in SLO window.
Kyle: agreed. quick mitigation: scale down janitor replicas to 4 and set JANITOR_CONCURRENCY=8 for the rollout; also add a k8s PodDisruptionBudget so it doesn't spin up again. who can patch?
Monica: i’ll open a small patch to add env + a flag to prefer lazy-delete with `--rate-limit=200/s` for the scanner. PR in a few mins.
Evan: i scaled the deployment to 2 for immediate relief (manual scale in cluster). attach times already falling — cluster shows GPU attach latency from 190s -> 28s in the last 4m.
infra-bot: [INFO] runbook note appended: suppressed janitor concurrency and created temporary anti-thrash flag on 3267894390.
Sara: can we also add an alert for small-file churn (files_created_per_min > 100k) so this doesn’t surprise us again? and a dashboard for small-write IOPS from janitor processes?
Kyle: yes — will add a grafana panel and an alert threshold. also recommend a cron job to compact old caches into tarballs before deletion so janitor can remove big blobs instead of millions of inodes.
Monica: PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/janitor/pulls/412 — adds `--rate-limit`, `--lazy-delete` and env var. includes a migration job that deletes old-run-xyz in chunks (shard by inode mod).
Evan: ran one shard of the migration: `find /var/tmp/gpu-cache/old-run-xyz -type f -print0 | xargs -0 -n100 -P4 rm -f` — reduced filecount by ~250k in 2m, IOPS fell. will keep running overnight.
Sara: follow-up ops items: 1) add churn alert, 2) add prevention check in runtime to not create millions of tiny files in cache, 3) postmortem with runtime team.
Kyle: milestone for Dedicated/Fleet: ensure provisioning doesn’t rely on noisy local-cleaners — add attach-time SLO and fallback to different region/pool if nvme_util>80% for >5m.
Evan: confirmed GPU queue cleared, workloads resumed. leaving janitor throttled until the PR is live and the migration completes. thanks all :thumbsup:
Monica: filing postmortem and cost estimate — extra ops hours + increased transient CPU/io for migration. will upload to #postmortems tomorrow.
Sara: nice quick mitigation, we should doc the `--rate-limit` param in runbook.
Evan: adding note to runbook now.
Kyle: if anyone sees new hotspots ping here, we’ll re-open and escalate.
